chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them.

Two men testified before 'Ali, peace be upon him, against a man that he had stolen, so he cut off his hand. Then they came with another man and said, “We made a mistake; this is the one.” So he did not accept their testimony, and he made them liable for the blood-money of the first.

key_terms.الْأَوَّلِ: the first man who was initially accused
key_terms.دِيَةَ: financial compensation owed for wrongful bodily harm
key_terms.فَقَطَعَ يَدَهُ: so his hand was cut off as the legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam 'Ali عليه السلام rule when witnesses wrongly caused a man's hand to be cut off for theft?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial case before Imam 'Ali عليه السلام in which false or mistaken testimony led to wrongful punishment. When the witnesses later changed their claim, their new testimony was rejected, and they were held financially liable for the harm caused to the first man.
